elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The consent-free affiliate carve-out is limited to a “financially responsible affiliate,” so it does not permit assignment to every affiliate as required.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The added language states that no approval is required for an assignment by Client to a successor in a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The added language states that no approval is required for an assignment by Client to a successor in an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The added language states that no approval is required for an assignment by Client to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The original mutual affiliate carve-out remains operative, allowing TrueLink to assign to a financially responsible affiliate without Client's consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that “Client's approval of any assignment by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause unconditionally states that TrueLink shall not assign or transfer to a competitor of Client.

elements.element: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a termination right.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that no change of control of Client gives TrueLink any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: There is no general consent-free successor-assignment right for TrueLink; only assignments to financially responsible affiliates are exempted.

elements.element: Customer must give written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no written-notice obligation on Client for a successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor must give written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no written-notice obligation on TrueLink for a successor assignment.

elements.element: Consent is required for Customer assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: A Customer assignment to a financially responsible affiliate requires no consent even if the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Consent is required for Vendor assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: A TrueLink assignment to a financially responsible affiliate requires no consent even if the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignments other than successor assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause applies an express not-unreasonably-withheld standard to Client's approval of any TrueLink assignment for which approval is sought or required.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to Customer assignments other than successor assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: No reasonableness limitation applies to TrueLink's withholding of approval for Client assignments.

result.reason: The redline adds most of the preferred protections, but the untouched mutual affiliate carve-out still permits Vendor assignment without Customer consent and restricts Customer's affiliate right to financially responsible affiliates. The fallback is also incomplete because Vendor receives no general successor-assignment right, neither party has a written-notice duty, the affiliate carve-out bypasses consent for some non-successor assignments, and Vendor's consent is not subject to a reasonableness standard. The changes remain confined to assignment and change-of-control issues and do not negate unrelated terms, but the retained carve-out and the reference to Client approval of “any” TrueLink assignment create avoidable scope tension.
